highlights.description: Conifers and broadleaf evergreens stand out in winter

species.note: Colonies may appear less fuzzy as polyps contract more frequently in colder water, but still present on shells year-round.
Often contracted into a tight column shape during rough weather, but still present and occasionally extending tentacles during calm periods.
Less active in the coldest months. Often found in a more contracted state, appearing smaller and more wrinkled than in warmer seasons.
Colonies may appear less active and somewhat reduced, but perennial portions survive through New England's cold coastal waters.

highlights.description: Buds reveal which tree is which before spring arrives

species.note: Adult medusae are absent from the water column, existing only as tiny polyps attached to underwater surfaces.
Often contracted and less active, appearing as small bumps or mounds. Colonies may be harder to distinguish from surrounding growth, but the clustered pattern is still visible.
Often remains closed and inactive during coldest months, appearing as small bumps on rocks that are easily mistaken for barnacles or limpets.
Rarely observed from shore due to rough seas, but colonies continue to exist in deeper offshore waters throughout the cold months.
Rarely observed in surface waters during cold New England winters, likely in deeper waters or in polyp stage.
